## Projects

- [Twins for Change](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/hack4edu-twins-for-change/): First place in the ProFuturo challenges at Hack4Edu 2026. Offline-first AI tutor for bilingual Yorùbá–English classrooms that grounds Gemma 3 answers in a 15,791-row corpus with hybrid retrieval-augmented generation. Language models such as Gemma 3 4B often make things up when they answer in Yorùbá. Twins for Change grounds every answer in real data: it retrieves verified bilingual examples from a 15,791-row corpus and gives them to Gemma before it answers. Hybrid search: dense bge-m3 and keyword BM25 vectors in Qdrant, merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion; the top three documents are passed to gemma3:4b before it answers. Bilingual answers: the explanation is in Yorùbá, and key terms and the summary are in English. Verified sources: every answer shows the three corpus documents it was based on. Compare mode: plain Gemma and Gemma with RAG answer the same question side by side. Offline: after a one-time setup, everything runs on a single laptop. Corpus: 15,791 rows (Mathematics: AfriMGSM, GSM8K; Sciences and humanities: AfriMMLU; Reading comprehension: Belebele; Translation: MAFAND). Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/Hack4Edu_2026. Live site: https://www.twinsforchange.com/
- [Reimplementation of clickstream event sequence analysis model TRACE](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/trace-reimplementation/): Transformer-based user representation learned from attributed clickstream event sequences. Re-implements the TRACE architecture in PyTorch and evaluates it on alternative public e-commerce datasets, because the dataset used in the original TRACE paper is not publicly available. Result: 0.787 AUROC · 0.696 AUPRC for TRACE (multi-task), average over the ATC, SAT and MAP tasks on the OTTO dataset. Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/AAI_HSLU_TRACE. Research project report (PDF): https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/papers/TRACEPAPER_Report.pdf
- [Application of AI and Deep Learning to Genomic and Transcriptomic Data Analysis in Cancer](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/upsa-thesis-cancer-survival/): Bachelor's Thesis, Pontifical University of Salamanca (UPSA), July 2026. Application of AI and deep learning methods to genomic and transcriptomic data analysis in cancer. Data: TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq (RSEM) expression and clinical data from cBioPortal, study brca_tcga_pub2015 (Breast Invasive Carcinoma, TCGA, Cell 2015); 819 patients raw, 519 after preprocessing. Models: Cox Lasso, Cox Elastic Net, Random Survival Forest, DeepSurv, Cox-nnet. The two deep survival networks had the highest C-index on the held-out test patients: Cox-nnet was best (0.8750), followed by DeepSurv (0.8032). Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/UPSA_Thesis_Research. Thesis (PDF): https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/papers/TFG_ManuelFasRuiz.pdf
- [Paper-Reimplementations](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/paper-reimplementations/): PyTorch reimplementations of baseline and state-of-the-art machine learning and AI models. Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/Paper-Reimplementations. Papers:
  - 01 Sequence to Sequence Learning (Completed). Based on "Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks" (arXiv:1409.3215). PyTorch LSTM encoder-decoder baseline (weights initialized uniformly between -0.08 and 0.08, following the Seq2Seq paper) and a bidirectional-GRU encoder with additive (Bahdanau) attention, compared with BLEU and ROUGE.
  - 02 Attention Is All You Need (Completed). Based on "Attention Is All You Need" (arXiv:1706.03762). Decoder-only, GPT-style Transformer language model (about 11 million parameters) with token and positional embeddings, causal masked multi-head self-attention, feed-forward layers, layer normalization and residual connections, trained for next-token prediction on a dataset of William Shakespeare's works on an NVIDIA L4 GPU, following Andrej Karpathy's 'Let's build GPT: from scratch' tutorial.
  - 03 Predicting Issue Types with seBERT (Completed). Based on "Predicting Issue Types with seBERT" (arXiv:2205.01335). Fine-tunes a locally stored seBERT checkpoint (24-layer BERT encoder, hidden size 1024) with two binary heads, worth_automating and enough_information, on github-labels-annotated.csv using the Hugging Face Trainer.
  - 04 An Image Is Worth 16×16 Words (Completed). Based on "An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale" (arXiv:2010.11929). Encoder-only Vision Transformer in PyTorch: 16x16 patch embedding (224x224 images into 196 patches), learnable [CLS] token and position embeddings, pre-norm encoder blocks with multi-head self-attention and a GELU MLP; 12 layers, hidden size 384, MLP size 1536, 6 attention heads, about 21.5 million parameters; trained on an NVIDIA L4 GPU.
  - 05 Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data (Completed). Based on "Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data" (arXiv:2106.11959). Encoder-only FT-Transformer in PyTorch (Section 3.3 of the paper): a Feature Tokenizer turns each column into its own token, with an nn.Embedding per categorical column and an nn.Linear per continuous column, and prepends a learnable [CLS] token. No positional encoding is used, because column order has no meaning. Pre-norm Transformer encoder blocks with multi-head self-attention and a GELU MLP follow, and a linear head on the final [CLS] state predicts whether a driver files an insurance claim next year. Two sizes were trained from scratch on an NVIDIA A100 GPU: about 25.37 million parameters (8 layers, hidden size 512, 8 heads) and about 1.4 million parameters (3 layers, hidden size 192, 3 heads), with AdamW, batch size 2048, weight decay 1e-4, cosine annealing, early stopping (patience 5) and binary cross-entropy with logits.
  - 06 Switch Transformers (MoE) (Planned/in progress). Based on "Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity" (arXiv:2101.03961). The repository has no folder for this paper yet.
